title: External review of the worker's descriptors, the Windows pipe and secret pages

snapshot.workingTree: Not recorded by the review. The source of the working tree it read was that of 0b0aa7fd417e0d0c5d126c831bdffaebaa955977 (tree b19e768f11410e7ba325f1d79a70e0295d345b20): no commit changed the source between that one and the fixes.

included: Every library module, the systems' backends, the worker and its channel, protected stacks and the wiping of memory, by reading

findings.title: A worker is called clean without a look at what it holds when it comes to serve
findings.evidence: After `close_range` succeeded before `main`, the check returned true without a listing.
findings.reproduction: A program opens a file in `main` before it calls `serve`, on a kernel with `close_range`.
findings.expected: A worker that holds a descriptor besides its standard streams says its start was not clean and takes no request, as the documentation of `serve` says.
findings.observed: The worker reported a clean start.
findings.impact: A descriptor opened before `serve` stays usable after the isolation, which refuses only new ones: a way out of the worker that its report does not show.
findings.recommendedFix: Always list the open descriptors before the worker is called clean.
findings.requiredVerification: A worker with a descriptor of its own must report an unclean start.

findings.title: Any text in the worker's variable closes the inherited descriptors before main
findings.evidence: The function tested only whether the variable was set.
findings.reproduction: Start a program that links the crate with the variable set to an empty or malformed text and with an inherited descriptor above standard error.
findings.expected: A text that `serve` does not take leaves the program as it is.
findings.observed: Every descriptor above standard error was closed before `main`, and the program then ran as one that is no worker.
findings.impact: A program that got a descriptor from its parent, such as an activation socket, loses it.
findings.recommendedFix: Check that the variable holds a well-formed setting before closing.
findings.requiredVerification: A malformed text must close nothing; a setting must still close what was inherited.

findings.title: A process of the same user that takes the worker's pipe first stops the start
findings.evidence: The pipe's access list names the user, and the pipe has one instance.
findings.reproduction: Another process of the user opens the pipe between its creation and the worker's own connection.
findings.expected: The start of a worker does not depend on other processes of the user.
findings.observed: The parent found another process number, sent nothing, and the start failed.
findings.impact: Denial of service by a process of the same user. No secret is sent.
findings.recommendedFix: Name only the AppContainer in the access list, or use several instances or inherited handles.
findings.requiredVerification: On Windows: a client that takes the pipe first must not stop the start.

findings.title: The Apple section of the function that runs before main does not name its kind
findings.evidence: The link section was given as `__DATA,__mod_init_func`.
findings.reproduction: Build a worker for macOS with a toolchain that does not take the bare section name for one of that kind.
findings.expected: The function runs before `main` on every Apple toolchain.
findings.observed: Not observed: the Apple code had not run.
findings.impact: A worker that keeps what it inherited. It then lists the descriptors and reports an unclean start, so the failure is a worker that does not start.
findings.recommendedFix: Name the section's kind, or close the descriptors when `serve` is called.
findings.requiredVerification: On macOS: a worker must hold nothing of a descriptor its parent left open.

findings.title: Without /dev/null the worker's streams do not end when it serves no more
findings.evidence: The drop of the streams did nothing when /dev/null had not been opened.
findings.reproduction: A worker under a policy that refuses opening /dev/null stops serving and does not end.
findings.expected: The parent sees the end of the pipes when `serve` returns.
findings.observed: The pipes stayed open for as long as the worker lived.
findings.impact: A call of the parent waits for the worker's end.
findings.recommendedFix: Close the descriptors when /dev/null is not there.
findings.requiredVerification: A call to such a worker must fail at once.

findings.title: Anonymous secret pages may be joined into huge pages
findings.reproduction: A kernel that joins small pages into huge ones copies a secret's pages and frees the old ones as they are.
findings.expected: A secret's bytes stay on the pages it was given.
findings.observed: Not observed; the report reasons from the kernel's behaviour.
findings.impact: Copies of secret bytes in freed pages, within reach of whoever reads physical memory.
findings.requiredVerification: The mapping of a secret on anonymous pages must carry the flag.

observations.title: A closed secret's change of access reaches its pages only
observations.evidence: Every buffer has whole pages of its own between guard pages, so no two secrets share a page.
observations.reproduction: None: the report checked the invariant and found it sound.
observations.expected: Changing the access of one closed secret does not reach another.

observations.title: A secret made before the isolation lies in a process that can still be read
observations.evidence: Listed in the report's table as documented, without a section of its own.
observations.expected: A program isolates itself before it takes a secret.

remediation.evidence: The check reads the system's list of open descriptors every time: a worker that holds one above standard error, inherited or opened by the program since, says its start was not clean. `worker`: the program with a file of its own reports a clean byte of zero; seen failing without the fix.

The function that runs before `main` reads the variable by the rule of `serve` and closes nothing for any other text. `worker`: a program started with four texts that are no setting keeps the descriptor its parent left it; seen failing without the fix. That whoever sets the environment decides whether the program is a worker is stated in docs/TECHNICAL.md.

Mitigated: the parent puts off a client that is not the worker and listens again, and the worker keeps trying a busy pipe for a second, so that one connection by another program no longer fails the start (`worker`, Windows only: a thread takes the pipe first). Accepted: a process of the same user that takes the pipe again and again for that second still stops the start, and nothing is sent to it; docs/TECHNICAL.md, What is not covered. Such a process may end the worker in any case: the access list of the worker's process leaves that to its user. The user's entry stays in the pipe's list, since Windows checks a process in an AppContainer against the user's entries as well as the container's. Handles passed by inheritance are what AUD-001-SEC004 replaced.

The section is `__DATA,__mod_init_func,mod_init_funcs`: it names its kind, pointers to functions run before `main`, whatever the compiler and linker made before. The static had `#[used]` already, which the report took to be missing. Not run on macOS when this record was filed.

Where /dev/null could not be opened, the two descriptors are closed outright. `worker`: under a filter that refuses opening for reading and writing, a call to a worker that serves no more and lives on fails at once; seen failing without the fix.

A secret's anonymous pages are marked `MADV_NOHUGEPAGE` before they are locked. `secret_memory`: the mapping of such a secret has the flag and a work area's has not; both seen failing when the code is changed. A work area keeps the huge pages the system gives it, on purpose: a large computation is much slower without them; docs/TECHNICAL.md, What is not covered.

limitations: The review is a reading of the source: its report records no command, no environment and no commit.

Its descriptions of the crate's parts, in section 4 of the report, name mechanisms the crate does not have, such as a stack switched in assembly, a `zeroize_bytes` function and a job limit that ends the process with its job; no finding rests on them.
Its quotations of code are paraphrases: names such as `SHED_POINTER` are not in the source.
The fixes were run on Linux x86-64 only when this record was filed; the Windows and Apple changes were compiled and linted.

normalization.origin: A free-form report, filed in this repository's sequence when it arrived. The metadata, the identifiers, the categories, the statuses and the remediation are this record's; the findings' substance and severities are the report's.
